judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital is a precise list of principal amounts and series designations, but it ends by saying the Series 2004 Bonds are "sometimes referred to together herein as the 'Series 2004 Auction Bonds'", collapsing two defined terms into one without stating when each applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.3(f) separately deems any reference to "Bonds or Auction Bonds" to reach both defined terms, which suggests the drafters themselves saw the overlap; the resulting circularity is a minor rather than operative incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ertain duties set forth herein" is deliberately open-ended, but as a recital it merely points to the operative sections rather than defining any duty itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Sections 2.1(c), 2.3 and 2.4, which spell out BD's actual obligations, and I found no provision it pulls against.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The double carve-outs ("except as provided therein" and "except as otherwise provided therein") leave the recital's statement of the interest rate dependent entirely on an external document, though the operative mechanism is not created here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 2.1(a)'s statement that the Auction Procedures determine Auction Rates, and I found no provision inconsistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital is a definite factual statement of appointment and direction, citing a specific section of the Auction Agreement; no term is meaningfully open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 3.1(a), which confirms the Auction Agent acts solely as agent of the Trustee, and with the preamble's description of the Auction Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line factual recital that the Auction Procedures need one or more Broker-Dealers; nothing in the wording admits of competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Section 2.1(c), which contemplates other Persons executing Broker-Dealer Agreements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The saving phrase "unless the context clearly requires otherwise" is an express invitation to argue over which references are to beneficial interests, and "clearly requires" has no fixed boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Section 2.6's Agent Member delivery mechanics and I found no contradicting provision, though the deeming rule could complicate reading of ownership terms elsewhere.
judgments.clause_name: 1.3(e) References to purchase, sale or holding

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule equates "Bonds" and "Auction Bonds" with both defined series terms, which is close to circular given the recital already merged those labels, but the second sentence (separate application per series) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the recital defining Series 2004 Bonds and Series 2004 Auction Bonds as the same instruments; the overlap is untidy rather than a genuine conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard authorization-and-enforceability warranty with conventional assumptions; every operative term is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the signature block and with Section 5.6's execution formalities; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The purpose statement and definition of "Auction" are definite, resting on defined terms (Auction Period, Initial Periods) supplied by the Indenture.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Indenture recital on Auction Rate determination and the schedule in Section 2.3(a); nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blanket incorporation "in their entirety" of documents not reproduced here leaves the content of the incorporated Auction and Settlement Procedures outside the four corners, a known source of scope argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(b) limits the Auction Agent's duties to those expressly set forth or expressly incorporated by 2.1(b), which harmonises rather than conflicts; the incorporation could nonetheless import terms cutting against Section 5.4's entire-agreement language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ssumes the obligations of, and limitations and restrictions placed upon, a Broker-Dealer" is broad, and the final sentence's reference to "applicable securities laws and rules" imports an undefined external standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 2.1(d) on own-account participation and the recital contemplating multiple Broker-Dealers; no contradiction identified.
judgments.clause_name: 2.1(c) BD agrees to act as Broker-Dealer

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permission, the Company's power to prohibit own-account Bids, and the affiliate carve-out are each stated with definite mechanics (notice, Hold and Sell Orders preserved).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The disclaimer of Auction Agent monitoring duty aligns with Sections 3.1(a)-(b); I found no provision it contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed deadline and defined subject matter (All Hold Rate, Auction Index); the only softness is "other electronic communication acceptable to the parties."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is restated identically in the Section 2.3(a) schedule, so the two provisions reinforce each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ustomers that it believes are Existing Owners" imports BD's subjective belief, and the disclosure carve-outs (including exposure to "loss, liability, claim, damage or expense") are broadly worded against the confidentiality promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The confidentiality undertaking runs to the Trustee, Issuer, Company and BD, which is consistent with Section 5.5's beneficiary scheme; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]s of the opening of business on such date" is grammatically detached and could refer to the Auction Date or the preceding Business Day, a small but real ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere fixes the reference date; the schedule in 2.3(a) does not address this notice, so the fit is neutral.
judgments.clause_name: 2.2(c) Notice of change in principal amount

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The BMA sentence sets an 11:30 a.m. Submission Deadline "instead of 1:00 p.m." while the table below still prints 1:00 p.m., and "the notice set forth in Section 2.4 will occur earlier" fixes no time; the OCR-garbled table adds to the uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4(b) requires notice of schedule changes and 2.2(a) restates the 9:30 a.m. step, so the internal tension is between this provision's own text and its table rather than with another section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(and thereby achieving the lowest possible interest rate on the Series 2004 Auction Bonds)" states a purpose that could be read as an obligation, and "other relevant documents" is an open-ended category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section 5.10 (no implied duties on the Company) and 2.1(c), the parenthetical could be pressed as a covenant the rest of the instrument does not support.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The no-netting requirement is precise; the only flaw is the OCR-run "EXHIBIT Borin" and the flexible alternative of "such other form as may be reasonably acceptable to the Auction Agent."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.4(a)'s reporting on Orders submitted by BD; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two notice obligations are tied to specific exhibits and a hard 3:00 p.m. cut-off; wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(a) expressly cross-refers to this subsection for departures from Auction results, so the two mesh.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As soon as reasonably practicable" and "if so requested" are soft, but the core notification duty and its trigger are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the final line of the 2.3(a) schedule and paragraph (a) of the incorporated Settlement Procedures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence notice duty with a specific cross-reference; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the notice requirement already stated in Section 2.3(a) but adds no inconsistent timing, so the two are cumulative.
judgments.clause_name: 2.4(b) Notice of change in Auction schedule

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]ake such other action as is required of BD pursuant to the Settlement Procedures" is a catch-all whose content lies outside this document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 2.1(b)'s incorporation of the Settlement Procedures, which supplies the content; no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duty is defined entirely by reference to Section 2 of the Auction Agreement, which is definite even though external.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the recital describing the Auction Agreement and with Section 3.1(b)'s express-duties limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]s calculated below" and the adjustment mechanism ("may be adjusted from time to time with the approval of the Company upon a written request of the Broker-Dealer") leave unclear whether the Company may refuse or must act reasonably.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2.5(b)'s formula and the Bond Insurer's back-up payment right, the fee scheme hangs together; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is long but mechanical; the one glitch is the reference to the Broker-Dealer definition "contained in the Series 2004 Auction Bonds" where Section 2.1(c) says the definition is in the Indenture.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mismatch with Section 2.1(c)'s "definition of 'Broker-Dealer' contained in the Indenture" is a real, if narrow, internal inconsistency about where the governing definition sits.
judgments.clause_name: 2.5(b) Calculation and payment of Broker-Dealer Fee

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence option in favour of a non-signatory; "right to pay" is clear and confers no obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with Section 5.5 making the Bond Insurer a third-party beneficiary and with 2.5(b)'s Company payment duty.
judgments.clause_name: 2.5 Bond Insurer right to pay fee

judgments.reasoning_cat1: BD's duty to "promptly deliver such funds" when a customer fails is one-sided but stated in definite terms, with the non-release sentence spelling out the consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers correctly to 2.3(d) and dovetails with 2.6(b)'s disclaimer and 3.1(b)'s express-duties limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat disclaimer naming four specific parties and one category of failure; the closing "or otherwise" is a small catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.6(a)'s allocation of settlement risk to BD and with Section 3.1's liability provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statement that the Auction Agent "owes no duties, fiduciary or otherwise, to any other Person" is categorical, though "or in the Auction Agreement" is grammatically awkward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble states the parties agree "for the benefit of the Existing Owners and the Potential Owners," which sits uneasily with a total disclaimer of duties to any other Person.
judgments.clause_name: 3.1(a) Auction Agent solely agent of Trustee

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An express-duties-only clause with a precise cross-reference to 2.1(b); the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It harmonises the broad incorporation in 2.1(b) with the Auction Agent's limited role in 3.1(a); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two sentences set overlapping and arguably different standards — no liability absent "negligence or misconduct," then no liability for good-faith errors unless negligent in ascertaining facts — and "misconduct" is undefined (wilful or not).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 3.2(d), which is absent from the executed text supplied, and otherwise sits with 3.1(b) and (d); the missing cross-reference is a modest fit problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item (i) is grammatically tangled ("shall not be: required to and does not make any representations") and "indemnity satisfactory to the Auction Agent" is a subjective standard, but the three exclusions are individually intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(a)-(c) and with 2.2(b)'s indemnity condition on disclosure; no contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The illustrative list following "including without limitation" breaks off mid-item at a semicolon, so the enumerated categories are incomplete and the reach of the general "circumstances beyond its reasonable control" against the truncated specifics is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 3.1(c)'s negligence standard, a force majeure excuse could be argued to overlap or override it, but no direct conflict is stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The addresses are specific, and "effective ... when such telecopy is transmitted" is a clear rule, but the notice list as presented omits BD and the Auction Agent while still requiring communications by a BD Officer and Authorized Officer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Issuer's notice address is "HOSPITAL SERVICES CORPORATION," whereas the recital defines the Issuer as the New Mexico Hospital Equipment Loan Council — a direct mismatch between operative notice text and the definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is internally strained: it makes the "entire agreement" consist of this Agreement plus an unenumerated set of "other agreements and instruments executed and delivered in connection with the issuance," and excludes understandings that are "oral, written or inferred" relating to the undefined "subject matter hereof."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with Section 2.1(b)'s wholesale incorporation of the Auction and Settlement Procedures and with Section 5.10's no-implied-duties rule, and the open-ended reference to other transaction documents makes the integrated whole indeterminate — a live basis for argument about extrinsic representations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The double "other than" construction (no Person other than the Auction Agent, Bond Insurer and BD, "other than the rights expressly granted to the Issuer herein") is awkward and leaves the Issuer's carve-out uncertain in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Company is a signatory with express obligations and rights (Sections 2.1(d), 2.3(a), 2.5), yet this clause omits it from the list of persons with enforceable rights and from the binding/successors sentence — a genuine incoherence with the preamble's reference to the benefit of Existing and Potential Owners as well.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amendment formality is precise: writing signed by each party's authorized representative plus written consent of the Issuer and Bond Insurer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.5 and 5.6(b); the only mild oddity is requiring Issuer consent when 5.5 limits the Issuer's rights, which is not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard non-waiver sentence limited to subsequent breaches; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with 5.6(a)'s requirement that waivers be in writing and I found no contrary provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary severability wording with no undefined terms or catch-all tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of the instrument; nothing depends on it in a conflicting way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the signature block and 5.6(a)'s writing requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he United States District Court in the County of New York" designates a court that does not exist by that name, and the sentence is grammatically broken ("the parties agree that all actions ... shall be brought in ... and that, in connection with any such action or proceeding, submit to the jurisdiction"), leaving both the identity of the forum and whether the designation is exclusive open to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument fixes a forum, but the clause purports to bind "the parties" while Section 5.5 denies enforcement rights to persons other than the Auction Agent, Bond Insurer and BD, complicating who is held to the forum and jury waiver.
judgments.clause_name: Section 5.9 — Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Waiver of Trial by Jury

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow no-implied-duties statement directed at the Company, with clear reference to this Agreement, the Indenture and the Auction Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 3.1(b) for the Auction Agent and does not contradict the Company's express duties in 2.5(b); the only tension is with the purposive language in 2.3(b), which addresses BD rather than the Company.
